brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

finish.summary: Seven full bases in a honeycomb flower at level 0, centre (0,0) plus its six neighbours. The centre is joint-bolted to each ring cell, every top face has a cover, and all 18 outside edges have caps. check_build shows no issues and meshClash reads clear. Total is 38 parts.

requirements.evidence: There are 7 full pieces: the centre (0,0,0) and its ring (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,-1), (0,1), (1,-1), (1,0). Six joint bolts (jointBolt:0#0,0#0 to 0#5) join the centre to each ring cell, and the LOOSE_BODY warnings stopped after the sixth. The ring-to-ring joints have no bolts; they weren't needed for the build to count as connected.
All 7 cells have a top cover (cover:*;full;top).

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge finished with caps
requirements.evidence: The configurator offered 18 cap sockets, one for each open outside edge, and all 18 caps are placed (cap:...;*;bearing). No cap sockets are left open.
check_build shows ok, no issues, and meshClash reads clear.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
